title: Encrypted persisted chat attachments + structured base64 outbound
problem: Chat images dropped/pasted into the composer were written as plaintext files under ~/Library/Application Support/Trinity S3AI/Attachments/. The UI preview and outbound request both read from those plaintext paths, and the server fell back to filesystem_read for image content.
root_cause: ChatAttachmentImporter.persistImageData wrote raw NSItemProvider data directly to disk and ChatComposerAttachment had no encryption flag or decrypt helper. ChatPanelView preview used NSImage(contentsOf:) on the plaintext path, and ChatViewModel.sendMessage only knew about a single text field with embedded <local_attachments> paths.
fix: Extended ChatComposerAttachment with isEncrypted (default false) and a loadDecryptedData() helper backed by TriOSEncryption(keyName: "attachments"). Updated ChatAttachmentImporter.persistImageData to AES-256-GCM encrypt the image bytes before writing. Updated ChatPanelView.attachmentPreview to decrypt in memory and render via NSImage(data:). Split composer attachments into image vs file in triggerSend; image attachments are decrypted, base64-encoded, and passed to a new ChatRequestBuilder attachments field that emits structured {kind, mediaType, dataUrl} entries matching the existing BrowserOS agents.ts contract. Fixed ChatAttachmentImporterSafePathTests and added ChatAttachmentEncryptionTests and ChatRequestBuilder attachment tests.

tests.swift_test: SKIPPED (XCTest not available in CommandLineTools-only environment)

variants.A: Minimal: encrypt only dropped/pasted image data, leave file attachments and MemoryStore plaintext — fast, closes the highest-risk gap.
variants.B: Balanced: encrypt image attachments + structured base64 outbound + preview decryption + tests — implemented, server never reads a plaintext image file.
variants.C: Comprehensive: add SQLCipher to MemoryStore, encrypt file attachments by copying them into the encrypted attachment directory, and rotate per-conversation attachment keys.

lessons: A small model flag (isEncrypted) preserves source compatibility while letting all callers treat encrypted and legacy plaintext attachments uniformly.
Reusing the existing TriOSEncryption named-key helper keeps the key lifecycle (generation, backup exclusion, 256-bit AES-GCM) consistent across analytics, conversation, and attachments.
The BrowserOS server already accepted structured image attachments, so the client-side change to emit them removed the need for server-side filesystem access for images.
Preview and outbound pipelines must both decrypt; if only one is updated the UI looks correct but the request still leaks plaintext or fails.
